source.title: On Evaluating the Durability of Safeguards for Open-Weight LLMs
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Boyi Wei; Nicholas Carlini; Yangsibo Huang; Tinghao Xie; Luxi He; Matthew Jagielski; Milad Nasr; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

page_placements.theme: Behaviour analogue: refusal/safety training and harmful-behaviour unlearning undone by fine-tuning, ablation, priming and jailbreaks

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; the text ends after the appendix material.
record.tranche_reason: Its own fine-tuning and prompt-template evaluations show recovery or evaluation sensitivity that challenges broad claims of durable unlearning, while also identifying settings where recovery is not observed.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported fine-tuning recovery for RepNoise and TAR, plus TAR WMDP results under altered prompt templates and answer extraction. Related-method descriptions and cited results are not recorded as rows. No direct activation-direction ablation, quantization attack, or robustness-to-attacks method is tested.
record.test_reason: Re-evaluates TAR, a tamper-resistant unlearning method not among the originals. Small fine-tuning changes recover WMDP-Bio accuracy to near the undefended level, including fine-tuning on the non-targeted retain set. Prompt-format changes raise TAR-Bio-v1 accuracy well above chance, and utility collapses on several benchmarks. The authors argue these methods hide rather than delete knowledge. TAR is itself a counter-method claiming robustness to these attacks, so version F is tested too.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add these points. The authors say TAR-Bio-v2 resists the prompt-template change but over-suppresses benign biology and collapses on GSM8K, BBH and HumanEval. They say WMDP accuracy can be uncorrelated with true unlearning. They say TAR's apparent robustness may rest on early-step fine-tuning instability. Their main thrust is that durability claims are hard to evaluate and should be narrowed to explicit threat models.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates RepNoise and TAR safeguards, not the gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU methods named in the broad claim. It uses fine-tuning attacks, benchmark evaluations, and prompt-format variations rather than reproducing one of those methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery varies with random seed, fine-tuning trainer, learning-rate schedule and warmup, fine-tuning paradigm (full-parameter versus LoRA), and for TAR-Bio-v1 with prompt template, BOS token, and answer-extraction method. TAR-Bio-v2's WMDP-Bio accuracy is comparatively stable across the four logits-order prompt formats tested.

fits_no_version.finding: RepNoise (Llama-2-7B-Chat) regains undefended-level harmful-request compliance after harmful fine-tuning with reseeding or the HF trainer. It also largely regains it after 100 benign AOA or Alpaca Salient examples, and on disjoint BeaverTails sets (Fig 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-noising defenses do not durably suppress harmful-request compliance: harmful or even 100 benign fine-tuning examples restore it.

record.problems: Many fine-tuning and Figure 7 results are presented graphically without numeric values in the text. RepNoise's original train/attack and test sets overlap substantially (75.3% of test elements also appear in training and attack sets), and the authors identify implementation and dataset-filtering issues in the original code. TAR prompt-template results depend on answer extraction; some results use model judges. The reported testing covers only two safeguards and a constrained set of attacks and prompts.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted due to the 60-row limit. Utility benchmark regressions, benign-biology perplexity, and broader safety side effects are not included because they do not directly measure the recovery attacks or prompt-only recovery named in the claim.

untested.parts: Only TAR is tested on targeted knowledge; RMU, gradient ascent, WHP and NPO are not tested.
No very small relearning sets (e.g. tens of facts or a held-out subset of forgotten facts) for TAR; RepNoise's 100-example result is on a different construct.
Entire version: no activation-direction ablation or internal analysis (loss/gradient-norm curves only).
Only chat template, BOS token and answer extraction were varied. No jailbreaks, rephrasing, other languages or in-context information.
Only TAR among knowledge-unlearning counter-methods; no attacks other than fine-tuning and prompt format.

missing.what: Utility of TAR-Bio-v1/v2 vs Llama-3-8B-Instruct: MMLU 65.7→55.7/55.0, GSM8K 74.4→1.5/4.8, BBH, HumanEval, MT-Bench, TruthfulQA; plus BenignBio perplexity 3.8→16.4. These bear on A's 'keeps general ability' and were wrongly left out.
TAR-Bio-v2 recovery on WMDP-Chem and WMDP-Cyber after forget-set and retain-set fine-tuning
Orig-Config 1-3 on the HF SFT trainer for TAR-Bio-v2 (more stable, successful attacks)
TAR-Bio-v2 with chat template plus GPT-4o/human extraction (no accuracy spike)
Undefended Llama-3-8B-Instruct WMDP-Bio per prompt format (71.1, 56.5, 73.2, 50.2) as baselines for r22-r31

record.verdict_notes: The RepNoise rows measure harmful-request compliance rather than targeted knowledge, so they are moved to fits_no_version rather than linked to A/B. TAR is a tamper-resistant unlearning counter-method, so its fine-tuning rows also bear on F, which the record marked as untested. Several TAR rows report best-of-5-seed values. Rows r13-r15 partly duplicate r10-r12. Cited results from the original TAR paper (e.g. about 45% for Orig-Config 2) should not be treated as this study's values.

versions.untested_parts: The study evaluates targeted benchmark performance and some utility benchmarks for RepNoise and TAR, but does not establish performance across all general abilities or all unlearning methods named in the claim.
Recovery is tested for RepNoise and TAR in the reported settings; it does not test every kind or size of unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact training set.
No activation-direction ablation or direct internal analysis demonstrating an access-blocking mechanism.
Tests WMDP prompt-template and answer-extraction variations for TAR; does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
No newer method is tested for resistance to the attacks in the claim.
